feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: 'He's got to go': Hakeem Jeffries calls for Hegseth's removal but stops short of impeachment
entry.summary: Speaking with Morning Edition, Hakeem Jeffries discussed ending the Iran war, holding Trump accountable and calls for new Democratic leadership, but offered few specifics on how Democrats would deliver.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: The Labor Department to release October jobs report Friday, what tactics are available to the Democratic Party to bring down fuel prices, judge blocks construction of Trump's arch for 14 days.

entry.title: Dearborn, Michigan, mayor on city's record turnout and the election of Abdul El-Sayed
entry.summary: NPR host Leila Fadel speaks with Abdullah Hammoud, the mayor of Dearborn, Michigan, about why his city turned out in record numbers to elect Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate.

entry.title: Head of Justice Department's Civil Rights Division resigns
entry.summary: The head of the Department of Justice Office of Civil Rights resigned on Thursday.

entry.title: It could be days before the winner of Mississippi's U.S. Senate race is declared
entry.summary: Votes are still being counted in Mississippi to see if Democrat Scott Colom will hold onto his lead over incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

entry.title: Trade unions join growing protests in France
entry.summary: Demonstrations continued across France Thursday, as trade unions went on strike over the cost of living.

entry.title: Voters rebuke Trump administration's ICE raids and immigration policies at the polls
entry.summary: ICE raids weighed heavy on the minds of voters this midterm election, especially those in border counties.

entry.title: The U.S. economy added far more jobs in October than expected
entry.summary: Employers added 165,000 jobs last month, the Labor Department said on Friday, blowing past economists' expected gains of around 59,000 jobs.

entry.title: Economist on the midterm results and the U.S. economy
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody Analytics, for analysis of the post-midterm election economy.

entry.title: Voters under 30 helped drive Tuesday's blue wave
entry.summary: Young voters played a large role in Democratic wins in this week's midterms. People under 30 voted blue at much higher rates than in 2024.
